NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk on Thursday described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a “beacon of hope” amid global uncertainty and said he was proud to call him a friend, while highlighting the absence of conflicts of interest between India and Poland as the two countries seek to strengthen their strategic partnership.Addressing a joint press conference with PM Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, Tusk said the two countries had held fruitful discussions on expanding bilateral cooperation and building on the strategic partnership established during Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.“We had a fruitful discussion with Prime Minister Modi about how Poland and India can develop and strengthen their strategic partnership. The decision to establish this partnership was made jointly during Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Warsaw in August 2024,” Tusk said.“The synergies between Poland and India are quite clear. We have no conflicts of interest and no historical issues that divide us. We are building our friendship on the basis of trust, shared values, and ideas such as non-violence,” he added.Tusk also drew a parallel between Poland’s Solidarity movement and India’s tradition of non-violence, saying the Polish movement had been inspired by such principles.Praising PM Modi’s role on the global stage, the Polish prime minister said India’s leadership offered hope at a time of geopolitical uncertainty and instability.“Someone like you, Prime Minister, leading a country as powerful as India, is a beacon of hope for all of us. I am very proud, truly proud, to be able to call myself your friend, Mr. Prime Minister,” Tusk said.He also pointed to the economic progress made by both countries over the past 35 years.“Over the past 35 years, both our countries have experienced unprecedented economic success and dynamic growth. Let me put it straightforwardly, without any doubts or hesitation: the world looks upon us with envy, at how India is developing and at Poland’s development,” he said.PM Modi said the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had expanded opportunities for economic cooperation between India and Poland, building on the momentum in bilateral relations over the past two years.“Our growing economic strength has created new opportunities for the India-Poland partnership. And the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement has made these opportunities even broader,” PM Modi said.The two leaders witnessed the exchange of key memoranda of understanding before addressing the joint press conference.Welcoming Tusk, PM Modi recalled his visit to Poland in 2024, when the two countries elevated their relationship to a strategic partnership.“During that visit, we elevated our relations to the level of a Strategic Partnership. Building on this strong foundation, our partnership has gained new momentum over the past two years,” Modi said.He also highlighted the historical ties between the two countries, describing their friendship as rooted in shared humanity and empathy rather than diplomatic relations alone.“The friendship between India and Poland is not based merely on diplomatic relations, but on the shared heritage of humanity and empathy,” Modi said.Recalling the assistance extended to Polish families during the Second World War, PM Modi said the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter to thousands of Polish children and families in India.The prime minister also said the two sides had agreed to strengthen cooperation in culture, education, sports and tourism. He added that they had discussed regional and global developments, democratic values and the need to reform global governance institutions.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace,” PM Modi said.Tusk arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for an official visit from October 21 to 23, at PM Modi’s invitation. He is accompanied by Poland’s minister of finance and economy Andrzej Domanski and a business delegation.The two prime ministers held delegation-level talks at Hyderabad House to review bilateral relations and explore cooperation across trade, defence, technology, space and other areas.India’s delegation included external affairs minister S Jaishankar, national security adviser Ajit Doval and foreign secretary Vikram Misri.Earlier on Thursday, Tusk paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat, laying a wreath at the memorial. Jaishankar also called on the Polish prime minister to discuss ways to deepen bilateral cooperation.In a post on X, Jaishankar said, “Pleased to call on Prime Minister Donald Tusk @donaldtuskof Poland. Appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India - Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains.”During his visit, Tusk is scheduled to attend the India-Poland Business Forum in New Delhi before travelling to Bengaluru on October 23 for engagements with leaders from India’s information technology and space sectors.Former Polish ambassador to India Adam Burakowski has said both countries aim to increase annual bilateral trade from approximately $6 billion to $10 billion.He has also identified defence and space technology as key areas for cooperation and pointed to the India-EU trade agreement as an opportunity to expand economic engagement.Tusk’s visit marks the first visit by a Polish prime minister to India since 2010. The two countries established their strategic partnership during PM Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.
Article Summary: Poland's PM Donald Tusk and Indian PM Narendra Modi held a joint press conference in New Delhi on Thursday. Tusk said the two countries had held fruitful discussions on expanding bilateral cooperation and building on the strategic partnership established during Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.

Article Title: State by state, some SIR hurdles are falling
Article Text:
SIR 2026 in Jhahhar

From queues to doorsteps

Then vs now

Less searching through old rolls

Chhattisgarh SIR drive

Finding the voters left out

When the usual apers are missing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With inputs from Arvind Chauhan, Kaushik Pradhan, Nisha Nambiar, Alok K N Mishra, Abhay Singh, Saptarshi Banerjee, Ashok Pradhan, Kautilya Singh, Lisa Monteiro, Amarjeet Singh, Rashmi Drolia, Navjeeven Gopal, Manvir Saini, Sreerag P S, K Krishnachand, Jignesh Parmar and Kapil Dave

For booth-level officers in Goa, enrolling a voter no longer involves one particularly tedious search: tracing the elector or a parent in the electoral rolls of 2002. That requirement has gone from the current registration process. The papers needed to establish eligibility have not.In Dehradun, Vibhanshu Bhatt, the BLO for Ajabpur, says a wider choice of supporting documents has made it easier to answer voters’ questions. A retired govt employee, for instance, can now offer documents other than a pension letter to establish their status.“With voters now having more options, it has become easier for us to deal with public queries and concerns,” he said.Across several states, BLOs are returning to households, collecting documents to resolve notices issued during the special intensive revision (SIR), and helping eligible voters left out of the rolls apply for re-inclusion. Some are working with a wider range of evidence. Others are helping applicants through the regular registration process, without the additional declarations or links to old rolls required during SIR.The states are at different stages, with officers handling pending verification, fresh enrolment or preparations for special summary revision (SSR). Nor has every state relaxed its documentary requirements. What connects much of the fieldwork is a more active effort to reach voters and help them complete the process.In Delhi, voters served notices because their details contained discrepancies or could not be linked to the 2002 roll no longer have to routinely queue for physical hearings at electoral offices. BLOs visit their homes and collect supporting papers. Assistant electoral registration officers can dispose of cases without formal hearings where the verification is sufficient.For daily-wage earners, the earlier visits to election offices meant losing work. Minor spelling differences, such as Narendra and Narender, are now being corrected without extensive documentation, officials said.“Officials have been directed to facilitate eligible voters rather than reject cases over procedural difficulties. However, prescribed eligibility requirements and documents remain applicable and BLOs do see documents such as birth certificate, passport wherever applicable before submitting declaration forms recommending disposal of cases,” an official said.By October 16, around 25 lakh of Delhi’s 33 lakh SIR notices had been resolved, against around 4 lakh by September 29.In Maharashtra , the BLO mobile application now has an “Other/Equivalent” option. Added after a proposal from chief electoral officer S Chockalingam, it allows supporting evidence beyond the 13 categories originally prescribed to be submitted for scrutiny.The provision is intended to help, among others, homeless people, particularly vulnerable tribal groups and sex workers who may lack the specified papers. Electoral registration officers (EROs) and assistant EROs assess the relevance and validity of the evidence.The numbers are substantial. Maharashtra issued notices to about 1.22 crore electors: roughly 59.76 lakh whose records could not be mapped to the previous roll and 62.48 lakh over logical discrepancies.BLOs can collect documents during home visits and upload them on ECINET for scrutiny. Where the evidence resolves the discrepancy, a routine personal hearing is no longer necessary. Further hearings can still be held when verification requires them.In Ahmedabad, engineering student Krisha Patel found that enrolling as a new voter required fewer papers than some of her friends had been asked to produce.“Unlike some of my friends who were asked to submit proof that their father or grandfather was a voter, I was asked to submit basic documents like Aadhaar card, birth certificate and photos.”Gujarat chief electoral officer Sandip Sagale said BLOs had been instructed to follow revised EC guidelines issued on Oct 15.“The documents establishing the relation of applicants to parents and grandparents are no longer mandatory according to the revised ECI guidelines. Registrations by first-time voters are very encouraging.”In Uttar Pradesh, chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa says current enrolment uses the regular statutory Form 6. Applicants no longer have to establish links with the 2003 rolls through their own names or those of parents or relatives.This is a return to the standard registration procedure after SIR, rather than a new nationwide concession. Rinwa said the original statutory Form 6 is being used during continuous updating of the rolls and will continue during SSR beginning Nov 12.Madhya Pradesh has also instructed district election officials not to seek a separate declaration with Form 6. Applicants must still provide the prescribed identity and address documents and make the form’s standard declaration that their information is true to the best of their knowledge.In Bengal’s current special enrolment drive, an official from the chief electoral officer’s office said applicants need not submit Annexure IV, the declaration used to establish family links with existing or previous rolls. BLOs continue to accept documents from the EC’s prescribed list.For Goa’s BLOs, removing the search through the 2002 roll eliminates a difficult step. But they say the documents for enrolment under Form 6 remain the same, whether someone is applying for the first time or seeking inclusion after deletion during SIR.For another set of BLOs, the immediate task is to return to names that did not make it onto the rolls.In Keralam, a drive that began on Oct 15 involves comparing pre- and post-SIR rolls to identify eligible voters omitted during revision. In Thiruvananthapuram’s Fort ward, BLO N Sajankumar is helping such voters seek inclusion. The exercise also involves checking information on deceased electors against local body databases maintained by the Information Keralam Mission.Chhattisgarh has supplied BLOs with booth-wise lists for a month-long drive to locate eligible omitted voters. They are making household visits, holding polling-station camps twice a week and organising separate camps at educational institutions for young voters.“BLOs are going door to door and, if a person earlier marked absent or shifted is now found, the Form 6 process is facilitated immediately,” a state govt official said. “But the documentary requirements have not been relaxed. The same standard documents applicable to an eligible voter continue to apply.”Completed applications and field-verification reports go to EROs for scrutiny. Finding a person at home does not, by itself, settle the application.In Ahmedabad’s Amraiwadi, special evening camps are scheduled from Oct 21 for night-shelter residents, labourers and homeless citizens, ahead of publication of the draft roll on Nov 12.Bihar is deploying 90,172 BLOs for a drive to enrol left-out voters and first-time applicants, with house-to-house searches and verification of records. The exercise is scheduled to finish by Nov 8.Odisha offers a measure of the additions already made. Since SIR, around 35,000 voters have been added to its rolls. Nearly 1,200 were eligible voters left out during revision; the remainder were newly enrolled voters. BLOs conducted door-to-door visits during a three-day drive from Oct 7 to 9, and registration continues till Oct 31.Delhi’s BLOs, meanwhile, have begun re-verifying 47.6 lakh people categorised as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate after they did not submit enumeration forms and were excluded from the draft rolls. Eligible voters found to have been wrongly excluded will need to apply through Form 6, with assistance from BLOs.In Jharkhand’s Khunti district, two tribal residents who lacked Aadhaar cards and conventional identity and address documents were enrolled after their eligibility was verified through land records, khatian documents and Gram Sabha testimony. Such evidence is subject to scrutiny by electoral registration officers, who decide applications on the basis of records available in each case.Chief electoral officer K Ravi Kumar has directed registration officers not to demand special or additional documents at SIR hearings and to consider available records where conventional proof is unavailable. Alternative verification has also been reported for vulnerable groups, including orphans, destitute women, residents of old-age homes and transgender persons.“Depending on the category, declarations, institutional certificates and field verification may be used,” Kumar said.BLOs can receive the evidence. EROs must examine it before deciding whether an applicant is eligible.In Dehradun’s Gandhigram, BLO Sarthak Srivastava said officers were finishing door-to-door checks of voters left off the roll, who now had more documentary options.In Goa, BLOs say residence proof remains a problem for tenants whose landlords refuse to give NOCs. Applicants must still furnish proof of residence, along with a birth certificate or school-leaving certificate.
Article Summary: BLOs can collect documents during home visits and upload them on ECINET for scrutiny. Applicants no longer have to establish links with their own names through the 2003 rolls. Minor spelling differences, such as Narendra and Narender, are now being corrected without extensive documentation.

Article Title: EC announces bypoll for Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat vacated by L Murugan
Article Text:
EC announces by-election for Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India (ECI) announced that the by-election to the Rajya Sabha seat from Madhya Pradesh, vacated by former Union minister L Murugan following his resignation, will be held on November 12. The counting of votes will take place on the same day, according to the commission’s press note shared on Thursday.The vacancy arose on October 14, when Murugan resigned from the Rajya Sabha. His term was scheduled to continue until April 2, 2030.According to the schedule announced by the ECI, the notification for the by-election will be issued on October 26. The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny of nomination papers will take place on November 3.Candidates will be able to withdraw their nominations until November 5.Polling will be held from 9 am to 4 pm on November 12, with counting scheduled for 5 pm the same day. The election process is to be completed by November 16, the commission said.The commission has specified the procedure for marking preferences on ballot papers, directing that only the integrated violet-coloured sketch pens supplied by the returning officer can be used.The ECI said in its press note, “No other pen shall, under any circumstances, be used in the above said election.”The commission has also said that observers will be appointed to monitor the election process and ensure that it is conducted freely and fairly.“Adequate measures for close monitoring of the election process by appointing observer shall be taken to ensure free and fair election,” the press note stated.
Article Summary: The by-election to the Rajya Sabha seat from Madhya Pradesh will be held on November 12. The seat was vacated by former Union minister L Murugan following his resignation. The election process is to be completed by November 16, the commission said.

Article Title: Why are uninsured vehicles not part of crash relief scheme? Supreme Court
Article Text:
Union road transport ministry officials said the scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With Centre formulating a scheme to provide interim financial relief of Rs 2 lakh to families of road crash victims for deaths and Rs 1 lakh for grievous injuries, limited to accidents involving insured vehicles, SC has sought an explanation from govt on why it is not being extended to uninsured vehicles.Taking note that “Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026” has not been notified or publicised, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan directed the govt to publicise it to ensure awareness. People must be made aware of their right to seek interim compensation, it said.Union road transport ministry officials said the scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act. Govt informed SC that the ministry shared the scheme with states and UTs on Feb 23. SC had directed the ministry in April 2025 to formulate the scheme.On why it covers only insured vehicles, officials said it was framed under provisions of MV Act dealing with insured vehicles. If the offender’s vehicle is uninsured, the matter will go to a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT).The apex court bench examined clause 6 of the scheme, which specifies that victims or legal heirs of the deceased can apply through a designated online portal, providing details of claims filed or pending before a MACT.Officials said that Section 164 of the Act, which deals with compensation in cases of death or grievous injury, requires the vehicle owner or insurer to pay Rs 5 lakh and Rs 2.5 lakh for death and serious injury, respectively, under the “no-fault liability” provision. A claimant need not establish that death or injury resulted from wrongful act, neglect or default on the vehicle owner’s part.“Hence, interim relief was set at Rs 2 lakh for death and Rs 1 lakh for serious injury for immediate relief. Final compensation would be higher, depending on the order of MACT,” an official said.
Article Summary: SC has sought an explanation from govt on why it is not being extended to uninsured vehicles. Centre formulating scheme to provide interim financial relief of Rs 2 lakh to families of road crash victims for deaths and Rs 1 lakh for grievous injuries. Union road transport ministry officials said scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act.

Article Title: At Jamnagar refinery, Rubio and Ambanis discuss energy, digital infra, giga factories
Article Text:
Marco Rubio, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor with Ambanis during a visit to RIL's Jamnagar Refinery Complex.

NEW DELHI: RIL chairperson Mukesh Ambani Wednesday showcased the conglomerate’s refinery along with initiatives in data centres and new energy giga factories in Jamnagar to US secretary of state Marco Rubio . But oil and gas remained the centrepiece of discussions at a time when US is grappling with soaring fuel prices and low diesel stocks.“Over the past year, India’s imports of US LPG have surged from under 10% to 67%, making US India’s largest LPG supplier. Reliance’s planned investment in the first new US oil refinery in 50 years is another major opportunity to expand American energy production and create jobs,” US ambassador to India Sergio Gor posted on X after the visit.US President Donald Trump had earlier announced the setting up of a $300 billion refinery in US, with RIL being part of his plank to revive industry in the country and bring back jobs that were offshored. The Mukesh Ambani-led company has, however, not outlined any details.The importance of Reliance has since increased because the Jamnagar complex is where hard Venezuelan crude can be refined. The takeover of Venezuelan oil reserves by US companies has been one of Trump’s bragging points.Rubio’s visit to Jamnagar came amid clear signals that US is interested in enhanced processing of Venezuelan crude. Outside US, RIL is the biggest user of Venezuelan crude.“This is a very large and prominent energy company. They also have a pretty large investment already in US. They have extensive refining capacity. As I highlighted (earlier), this is a company, for example, that has the capability to refine the heavy crude that’s produced in the western hemisphere, including from Venezuela, so I’m sure that’s a topic we’ll discuss. I think through our conversations, we’ll hopefully identify other opportunities to partner and work together,” Rubio said.In a statement, RIL said: “Secretary Rubio and Ambassador Gor were also explained Reliance’s New Energy giga-factories, which are currently being commissioned in phases, and the data centres under construction. The tour provided an overview of the company’s investments across energy and digital infrastructure, bringing together its well-established advanced manufacturing and deep-tech capabilities.”The talks, which included executive director Anant Ambani, also focused on the intersection of energy and digital infrastructure, including power supply for data centres.
Article Summary: RIL chairperson Mukesh Ambani showcased the conglomerate’s refinery along with initiatives in data centres and new energy giga factories in Jamnagar. But oil and gas remained the centrepiece of discussions at a time when US is grappling with soaring fuel prices and low diesel stocks.

Article Title: India deal pretty close, will be different: Trump; pact to exclude unresolved sectors
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump said that his administration was “pretty close” to a pact with India.

Deal may skip sectors where India, US unable to reach understanding

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Anticipation of an early trade deal with US rose higher on Wednesday when US President Donald Trump, after months of dillydallying, said that his administration was “pretty close” to a pact with India, though asserting that it will be different from other trade agreements.“They want to make a deal. We’re going to make a deal. Pretty close, yeah… It’s going to be a much different kind of deal than we’ve done,” Trump told reporters at Oval Office.His comments came hours after US secretary of state Marco Rubio said that the two countries are “as close as you can be without having an executed agreement”. Last week, commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal had said that the deal had almost been finalised and what remained was the legal vetting, while stating that it will be implemented once there was clarity on India’s competitive advantage.However, officials in Delhi were parsing Trump’s statement about the likely deal being different, and keeping their fingers crossed given the many twists and turns during the negotiations.There has been speculation in certain quarters that the much-awaited deal may not be comprehensive, covering all sectors, and the two sides may like to leave aside the issues which have been particularly nettlesome to have an understanding on those for which they have been able to hammer out agreements.Last year, Indian oil companies entered into agreements to import gas from US, and there are demands from American companies on specific technological products, which govt is willing to accept, provided these help secure easier access for locally produced textiles, footwear and engineering goods.A comparative advantage for India — a reference to lower additional tariffs on exports from the country — will depend on how the Trump administration uses the powers under the Trade Act to impose duties on imports from across the world.Currently, Indian exports to US face 10% additional tariffs, under Section 301, for govt’s alleged failure to check the import of goods made using forced labour, with the administration arguing that the “unfair” advantage acts as a barrier for US exports. Additional tariffs of 10-12.5% have been imposed on over 50 countries.The outcome of a second probe under the same provision related to structural overcapacity is awaited. Officials here indicated that clarity was required on some of the aspects and the assessment is that things will be clearer after the US mid-term elections, slated for the first week of Nov, for which Republicans have made the Trump administration’s claim to have secured higher protection for American business and labour one of their key planks.In Aug 2025, Donald Trump imposed a 50% tariff on Indian goods, including a secondary tariff of 25% for Russian oil imports, which was withdrawn.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump said that his administration was “pretty close” to a pact with India. “It’s going to be a much different kind of deal than we’ve done,” Trump told reporters at Oval Office.

Article Title: Cars to brake on their own: Centre plans AEBS mandate from Oct 2030
Article Text:
As for pre-2030 still-in production models, AEBS would mandatory from Oct 2032.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Certain safety features of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) will be made mandatory for cars, particularly taxis, as govt steps up efforts to reduce road crashes. From Oct 2030, all new car models would be required to be equipped with the advanced emergency braking system (AEBS), the most important ADAS feature, TOI has learnt.As for pre-2030 still-in production models, AEBS would mandatory from Oct 2032.The draft notification, with timelines for different ADAS safety features for cars, would be out soon, people aware of the development said, adding that focus would be more on taxis. They said the proposed timelines take into account the lead time that industry and users would need.ADAS is a set of more than 100 electronic technologies that increases safety by detecting potential hazards, warning the driver, and in some cases, automatically controlling brakes or steering to prevent a collision. At present, some cars have ADAS.Starting Jan 2027, new truck and bus models will have AEBS — it detects an imminent collision with a vehicle or obstacle and automatically applies brakes, if the driver fails to respond adequately, preventing a crash or reducing its severity.Blind spot information, moving off information and driver drowsiness detection and alert, and lane departure warning systems have been also made mandatory for these commercial vehicles.It’s learnt that features, including automatic command steering functionalities, emergency lane keeping system, drowsiness and attention warning systems, would be made mandatory for taxis.The introduction of these norms could initially focus on ensuring compliance with Automotive Industry Standards for vehicles already equipped with AEBS or more advanced systems that can intervene in steering and lane-keeping, said Automobile and mobility expert Rama Pandey. “These technologies could prove a boon for commercial drivers who spend hours behind the wheel. By shifting more safety-critical & fatigue-inducing driving decisions to automated systems, ADAS could make driving safer and less strenuous,” he added.
Article Summary: From Oct 2030, all new car models would be required to be equipped with the advanced emergency braking system (AEBS) As for pre-2030 still-in production models, AEBS would mandatory from Oct 2032. Draft notification, with timelines for different ADAS safety features for cars, would be out soon.

Article Title: Monsoon's gone, El Niño isn't: Why India's weather worries are far from over
Article Text:
What is El Niño and how does it affect India's weather?

Global impact of El Niño

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

El Niño is putting the world on alert, and India could be among the countries facing its next major weather test. After a monsoon marked by a 13 per cent rainfall deficit, attention is shifting to whether the climate phenomenon will bring a warmer winter, disrupt rainfall patterns and add to the pressure on agriculture.From Indonesia’s raging wildfires to an unusually active Pacific hurricane season, its effects are already emerging across the globe. Now, the question is what a strengthening El Niño could mean for India in the months ahead.According to the BBC, El Niño has been strengthening for several months and is already influencing weather patterns worldwide, with Indonesia experiencing its worst wildfire season since 2015, heightened hurricane activity in the eastern Pacific and reduced monsoon rainfall in India.The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned that the phenomenon could intensify further towards the end of 2026 and persist into 2027, raising concerns over its potential impact on temperatures, rainfall and extreme weather events across different regions.For India, the immediate concern is whether the strengthening El Niño will compound the effects of the deficient monsoon and influence winter temperatures, rainfall and agricultural conditions in the coming months.El Niño is a climate phenomenon characterised by unusually warm sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. It is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a natural climate pattern that influences atmospheric circulation, wind systems and rainfall distribution across the world.For India, El Niño is closely watched because it is generally associated with a higher risk of below-normal southwest monsoon rainfall.The warming of Pacific waters alters atmospheric circulation and can weaken conditions that support the Indian monsoon, increasing the possibility of prolonged dry spells and rainfall shortages.While central India received near-normal rainfall, eastern and northeastern India recorded a 26 per cent deficit, classified as an exceptional drought, while southern states received 24 per cent less rainfall than average, according to the BBC.A strengthening El Niño could contribute to warmer-than-normal conditions in parts of India, potentially increasing pressure on water resources and agriculture.The World Meteorological Organization (WMO), citing the South Asian Climate Outlook Forum, projected normal to above-normal maximum and minimum temperatures across much of South Asia during October–December 2026.Higher temperatures later in the winter could also threaten wheat yields if heat coincides with the grain-filling stage, although the impact will depend on actual weather conditions.However, conditions in January and February will depend on evolving climate patterns, including western disturbances.El Niño is expected to push temperatures higher across much of the world while shifting rainfall patterns, increasing the risks of drought, wildfires and flooding in different regions.In Southeast Asia, including Indonesia, hotter and drier conditions are raising wildfire and drought risks. In contrast, parts of East Africa could experience heavier rainfall and flooding, while drought risks remain a concern in other areas.El Niño is also influencing tropical storms. The eastern Pacific has experienced heightened hurricane activity, while stronger upper-level winds over the Atlantic have suppressed hurricane development.In South America, its effects vary, with drier conditions possible in parts of the Amazon and increased rainfall and flooding in some southern areas.
Article Summary: After a monsoon marked by a 13 per cent rainfall deficit, attention is shifting to whether the climate phenomenon will bring a warmer winter. The World Meteorological Organization has warned that the phenomenon could intensify further towards the end of 2026 and persist into 2027. The immediate concern is whether the strengthening El Niño will compound the effects of the deficient monsoon.

NEW DELHI: Road transport ministry has proposed raising the pass mark for safe-driving tutorial assessment from 60% to 75% and waiving fees for specified driving-licence services availed through online Aadhaar authentication, along with charges for changes to licence particulars such as name and address.The proposed changes to driving licence rules are aimed at tightening assessment requirements and to ensure availing licence-related services without any hassle. The changes proposed in the draft notification to amend sections of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules published late Wednesday night also seek to streamline online driving licence services, specify acceptable identity and residence documents, and introduce time limits for processing applications to change licence particulars.Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes. These include Aadhaar, passport, voter identity card, recognised educational certificates and birth certificates, among other documents. Electricity and household gas bills not older than three months are among the proposed address-proof documents.LIC policy would no more be accepted as a proof.The draft also provides for a consolidated application form covering services such as licence renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the SARATHI portal wherever available.In another proposed change, a vehicle class would be deleted from a driving licence within seven days of an application to surrender it. However, applicants permanently surrendering a class would not be eligible to obtain a learner’s or driving licence for that class for one year.The draft notification invites objections and suggestions from stakeholders within 30 days of publication. Article Title: Rosatom completes supply of engineered safety features actuation systems for Kudankulam N-plant units 3 and 4
Article Text:
​Kudankulam N-plant​

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Russia state atomic energy corporation Rosatom’s division Rosatom Automated Control Systems has completed the supply of equipment for engineered safety features actuation system computerised subsystems (ESFAS CS) for units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu. The role of the general designer and supplier of equipment in the project belongs to Atomstroyexport.In total, about 300 items of equipment were manufactured and delivered to the plant – four sets of ESFAS CS in accordance with the number of safety instrumentation and control trains, per each power unit featuring VVER-1000 reactors.ESFAS is the system that monitors the process parameters of a power unit when there is a deviation from normal operation conditions. In case of an accident, the system automatically initiates the start of safety instrumentation and control systems and sends commands to actuators (boron injection pumps and other active protection means) in order to prevent a beyond-design-basis accident and bring the reactor plant to a safe state. The system also ensures reactor cooldown, which is a controlled decrease of coolant temperature and pressure down to safe values after the shutdown.To avoid simultaneous failure, they are physically separated — located in different rooms — and have autonomous power supply from separate diesel generators.Specialists developing the ESFAS CS for units 3 and 4 relied on the operating experience of the same system at Kudankulam NPP units 1 and 2, which allowed them to implement a number of optimised solutions. One of such solutions is the application of non-programmable modules that process signals from sensors without the use of microprocessors. This helps to reduce the dependence of safety functions on application software and increases the resistance of equipment to potential common cause failures.The final delivery of ESFAS CS equipment was yet another step of equipping the power units with Russian automation, control and safety systems, implemented through industrial cooperation. Installation on the site will be followed by the pre-commissioning stage, which includes the off-line and integrated tests of the systems.Following the tests, the systems will be prepared for commissioning and further operation at units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam plant.Kudankulam plant features six power units with VVER-1000 reactors, with the total installed capacity of 6,000 MW. The first phase (units 1 and 2) was commissioned in 2013 and 2017, respectively. The second phase (Units 3 and 4) is under construction.
Article Summary: Rosatom has completed the supply of equipment for engineered safety features actuation system computerised subsystems (ESFAS CS) for units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu. ESFAS is the system that monitors the process parameters of a power unit when there is a deviation from normal operation conditions.

Article Title: NMC denotifies medical education rules; annual disclosures risk lacking verification

National Medical Commission has denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023. With the denotification, all specific penalties against medical institutions that fail to comply with any of the statutory provisions and regulations or minimum standards are no longer applicable.Any action taken while the regulations were in force would not be affected. However, NMC has not taken any action against many colleges flouting regulations as in the case of non-payment of stipend to MBBS interns and doctors doing PG. Colleges will now have little to fear if they do not pay stipend as the penalty for is not specified in the NMC Act.The Act only states that the Medical Assessment and Rating Board shall take such measures, including issuing warning, imposition of monetary penalty, reducing intake or stoppage of admissions or recommendation for withdrawal of recognition against a medical institution for failure to maintain the minimum essential standards specified.“Notwithstanding such denotification, the requirement of furnishing the annual disclosure report shall continue to operate” in accordance with relevant sections of NMC Act 2019, read the denotification announcement gazetted on Oct 14. NMC Act stipulates that the UnderGraduate Medical Education Board and the Post-Graduate Medical Education Board shall specify norms for compulsory annual disclosures by medical institutions.The 2019 Act also states that MARB may conduct evaluation of any institute at any time without prior notice. However, with the denotification, the aspects that need to be included in the evaluation report, such as verification of physical infrastructure, availability of the required number of faculty and review of feedback from students, have also been removed.Without evaluation by MARB, the mandated annual disclosure would just be claims by a medical college unverified by an independent assessment.
Article Summary: National Medical Commission has denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023. With the denotification, all specific penalties against medical institutions that fail to comply with any of the statutory provisions and regulations are no longer applicable. NMC has not taken any action against many colleges flouting regulations.

Article Title: Congress pulls up SBI over data breach, seeks accountability; experts call leak 'no ordinary incident'
Article Text:
SBI data leak: Personal details of 3,897 customers were identified on the dark web. Congress's media and publicity department head, Pawan Khera, questioned the bank's ability to detect the breach and its response towards affected customers.

'No ordinary incident': Expert flags security risks

SBI says customer balances are safe

SBI incident amid wider cyber threats

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday pulled up the State Bank of India (SBI) over the suspected exposure of 3,897 customer records on the dark web, demanding answers from the country's largest bank and accountability for those responsible. Cybersecurity law expert Pawan Duggal called the incident "no ordinary incident", warning that the exposure could have implications for India's national security.The criticism came after SBI said a preliminary analysis of around 3.75 lakh records available on the dark web had identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The bank said it was investigating the suspected exposure after receiving alerts on October 16 from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency, and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).Congress's media and publicity department head, Pawan Khera, questioned the bank's ability to detect the breach and its response towards affected customers."It is bad enough that the State Bank of India @TheOfficialSBI, the country's largest public sector bank, has suffered a data breach involving 3.75 lakh rows of data, with 3,897 records containing personally identifiable customer information -- including mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and loan-related details.""What makes this even more alarming is that SBI did not even detect the breach itself. An external agency had to alert the bank that its customers' data had already been published on the dark web," he said on X.Khera alleged that the bank had yet to inform customers whose personal information was exposed." A bank entrusted with the financial security of millions cannot afford such a catastrophic failure of data security, breach detection and customer accountability. SBI owes its customers answers. Those responsible must be held accountable," he asserted.Pawan Duggal, chairman of the International Commission on Cyber Security Law, said the suspected leak was particularly serious given SBI's size and the volume of sensitive information it holds."The SBI data leak is no ordinary incident. India is the world’s most populous nation. The SBI is the country’s largest bank, holding a volume of accounts unmatched by any other financial institution. A leak here involves far more than just names; it includes numerous government accounts, such as those of public sector employees, meaning a vast amount of sensitive government information is exposed. The intent behind such a leak is clear: state and non-state actors could exploit this data to negatively impact India’s sovereignty, integrity, and security. .. Section 79 of the IT Act mandates that intermediaries must exercise "due diligence" in the discharge of their functions. The central government has established specific rules, such as the IT Rules, 2021, and the IT Directions, 2022, that define what constitutes due diligence; it remains to be seen whether these requirements were met... It is high time for India to wake up; the country still lacks a dedicated national law on cybersecurity, and the existing Information Technology Act of 2000 does not adequately address these critical aspects..."The suspected exposure reportedly includes customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses and residential addresses. The records also contain branch and Customer Information File (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan and lead records and other related files.Responding to the incident, SBI said the suspected exposure had affected a very small number of customers and had not materially affected its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity."Customer balances are completely safe, and we are taking all possible steps to protect the interest of our valued customers," the bank said in a post on X.SBI said it had activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to investigate the alleged compromise.The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine the potential source and extent of the exposure, and assess the risks to customers and the bank."We reiterate that safety of our customers' financial assets, data and their trust in us remain our highest priorities," it said, adding that remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.The suspected data exposure comes days after CERT-In issued a 'critical' advisory warning that autonomous artificial intelligence agents had accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations without authorisation.In its advisory, titled 'AI Agents as Attack Vectors', the agency said some AI models and agents undergoing research and evaluation had exceeded the authorised scope of their tasks and accessed live systems. The agents reportedly used credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and overly permissive cloud service roles.CERT-In also reported a compromise involving private keys linked to eight intermediate certification authority certificates belonging to India-based certification authority eMudhra Ltd. The affected certificates included six Transport Layer Security certificates and two code-signing certificates.The agency warned that the compromised keys could be used to issue fraudulent certificates, impersonate legitimate websites and potentially intercept or modify encrypted communications.
Article Summary: Congress's media and publicity department head, Pawan Khera, questioned the bank's ability to detect the breach and its response towards affected customers. Cybersecurity law expert Pawan Duggal called the incident "no ordinary incident", warning that the exposure could have implications for India's national security. The suspected exposure reportedly includes customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses and residential addresses.

Article Title: India sees a drop in GHG emissions in 2025, even as UNEP flags huge gap in global reduction efforts
Article Text:
India sees a drop in GHG emissions in 2025

.Total GHG emission of the six largest emitters in 2025 in gigaton of CO2 equivalent (GtCO2e) per year.

Per capita GHG emission of the six largest emitters in 2025 in tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e) per person per year.

NEW DELHI: Rise in global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions may continue to pose a serious threat of global warming but India reported a decrease in its level of emission in 2025 over the previous year and its trend broke from a longer period of rapid growth, in part due to weather effects, but also due to the country’s “structural shifts towards renewables”, the UN Environment Programme has observed in its annual ‘Emission Gap Report’ released on Wednesday.The report shows that India is currently the third-largest emitter in terms of total GHG emissions but the country’s per capita emission is not only less than half of the global average but also substantially lower than the top two emitters - China and the US - where total emissions increased last year.Besides India, the EU (27 nations collectively) and Russia too reported decreases in their levels of emissions in 2025 when the total global emissions were similar to the 2024 levels.In terms of magnitude, the increase in the US far exceeded those of all other countries. The next largest estimated increases were in Türkiye (the host of the upcoming UN climate conference, COP31), Iran and Indonesia.Though the efforts are being made in most of the countries to reduce their carbon footprints, the report underlines that the temperature projections are still “far too higher” and the chance to keep global warming below 1.5 degrees Celsius with no overshoot is gone.It notes that if the current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8 degrees Celsius within this century over the pre-industrial levels (1850-1900) and increase thereafter.Flagging the huge gap in the emission reduction requirement, the report observed that the world is required to reduce the GHG emissions by 18% by 2030 and by 45% by 2035 from the 2025 levels to remain within the less devastating warming limit, but the full implementation of the current climate action pledges by all nations, put together, would only reduce emissions by 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035, relative to 2025 levels, leaving the countries more vulnerable to the disastrous consequences of climate change.“These outcomes are worse than last year’s projections due to the withdrawal of the USA from the Paris Agreement and revised estimates of historical emissions. New nationally determined contributions (NDCs) submitted since last year’s report have made a negligible difference for these projections,” it said.The report, while pitching for urgent emissions cuts to come back from an overshoot of 1.5 degrees C, notes that keeping peak warming below 1.7 to 1.8 degrees C (by mid-century) will quickly become impossible without urgent action. “Every five years of COemissions at current levels pushes peak warming up by around 0.1 degree C,” it said.“Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5 degree C increases climate impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year. So, we must pull out all the stops to minimize peak warming and return to 1.5 degree C by the end of the century,” said Inger Andersen, executive director of UNEP.The report looks at a ‘lowest possible’ 1.5 degree C overshoot scenario, in which peak warming is limited to 1.7-1.8 degree C. To get onto this pathway, global GHG emissions would have to be cut by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, relative to 2025 levels."Overshoot is not surrender. We can still keep it as small and as short as possible – and bring temperatures back below 1.5 degrees by the end of the century," UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in a message on the report.Collectively, G20 members increased their emissions by 0.7% in 2025. Under current policies, only six G20 members (China, India, Indonesia, Russian Federation, South Africa and Türkiye) are assessed as likely to achieve their unconditional 2030 targets, while the assessment of the European Union is inconclusive.“India also appears likely to achieve its 2035 target based on policies already in place. However, this should be interpreted differently, because India’s NDC is formulated as an emissions-intensity target,” says the report.The report notes that though the global GHG emissions in 2025 were similar to 2024 levels, CO2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion of oil, coal and gas, and nitrous oxide (N2O) and fluorinated gases (F-gases) emissions continued to increase last year while methane (CH4) emissions remained almost the same as in 2024."These increases were offset by a decrease in CO2 emissions from the land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) sector of about 0.5 gigatons of CO2 equivalent (GtCO2e). The decrease in LULUCF CO2 emissions was partially driven by a decline in biomass-burning emissions, including a decline in global wildfire carbon emissions in 2025, compared with the exceptionally active 2024 season," it said.
Article Summary: India is currently the third-largest emitter in terms of total GHG emissions. The country’s per capita emission is not only less than half of the global average but also substantially lower than the top two emitters - China and the US - where total emissions increased last year.

NEW DELHI: Flagging repeated lapses in television content, the information and broadcasting ministry has asked private satellite channels to check communal rhetoric, sensational coverage of crime and violence and the misuse of artificial intelligence in news production, warning that violations of the Programme Code could invite action.In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the ministry said its Inter-Departmental Committee had found content aired by various channels “not in conformity with the spirit of the Programme Code”. It also noted instances of similar news and visuals being broadcast across multiple channels on the same subjects.The committee stressed that “inappropriate behaviour or language should not be normalised in telecast”, and urged broadcasters to follow both the letter and spirit of existing rules.Taking particular note of television debates, the advisory said channels must ensure that discussions do not “promote or encourage communal or anti-national attitudes”. It called for careful selection and prior sensitisation of panellists, adequate editorial control and, where necessary, “immediate remedial measures such as muting, disclaimers, interruption or discontinuation of feed” to stop derogatory, abusive or inflammatory content from being aired.On AI, the ministry asked broadcasters to exercise caution while using it, including generative tools, for graphics and virtual news presentations. “The use of AI tools may be limited to assistive capacity,” it said, stressing that accuracy, authenticity and sensitivity must not be compromised.The advisory reiterated the prohibition on live coverage of anti-terror operations by security forces, restricting such reporting to periodic briefings by authorised officers. Telecasts of related visuals should be time-stamped wherever necessary to avoid misleading viewers.It also urged channels to avoid graphic or disturbing visuals, unverified and sensationalised crime reports, excessive replay of violent footage and coverage that might glorify unlawful behaviour. Images from disasters and major accidents, it said, should be time-stamped where necessary to prevent panic.Broadcasters were further reminded to use only authentic maps issued by the Survey of India and protect the identities of sexual offence victims, including through indirect details.The ministry asked channels to strengthen editorial reviews and train news, production and transmission staff in the Programme Code.

Article Title: ‘Next big challenge is drugs’: Amit Shah sets 2029 target after Naxalism crackdown
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Stating that peace had been established in the country's three primary hotspots -- Jammu and Kashmir , northeast region and areas affected by Left-wing extremism -- home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday said the home ministry is now focused on the next big challenge, the drug menace, and aims to make the country completely narcotics-free by Dec 31, 2029.Addressing an event here to mark the Police Commemoration Day, Shah said 2026 has been an extremely significant year for the Indian police, as they successfully freed the country from the decades-old stranglehold of violent Naxalism by March 31. "From 1981 to March 2026, the country had endured numerous hardships due to Naxalism....more than 3,600 security personnel were martyred, and nearly 13,700 innocent civilians also lost their lives," he recalled and said the sacrifices of 3,600 police personnel have laid the foundation of progress "as the country moves forward on the path of development".The Police Commemoration Day event was attended by Members of Parliament Krishna Prasad Tenneti and Rajiv Kumar, home secretary Govind Mohan, Intelligence Bureau director Mahesh Dixit and the Directors-General of various Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs).Stating that an environment conducive to development has emerged in Kashmir, northeast and LWE-hit regions, which now compete with the rest of the country in terms of development, Shah particularly thanked the CRPF and its CoBRA battalion as well as the Chhattisgarh police for their role in the decisive fight against LWE.Praising the police forces for always remaining on duty, irrespective of festivals or holidays, to strengthen internal security during elections, festivals, protests and also guarding the borders, Shah particularly appreciated the CAPFs for ensuring that the recent polls in West Bengal, given its long history of electoral violence, were uneventful with not a single fatality.Stating that several challenges remain, the home minister said the next top agenda for the home ministry is to dedicate the remaining part of 2026 and three years after that to freeing the country from the drug menace. Noting that drug abuse and trafficking undermine the future of coming generations, place an unnecessary burden on the economy and often provide financial support to organisations with anti-national intentions, Shah called upon police forces across the country to wholeheartedly join in implementing the 'nasha-mukt Bharat' roadmap.Meanwhile, to spread the message regarding the govt's time-bound war on drugs, the home minister flagged off a nationwide motorcycle rally on Wednesday with the theme 'fight against drugs'. Five riders each from 36 states/Union territories and 9 CAPFs are participating in this rally and will reach Kevadia, Gujarat, from different parts of the country, to join the Ekta Diwas parade on Oct 31.Police Commemoration Day is observed each year on Oct 21, to honour the 10 CRPF personnel who had bravely resisted an attack by Chinese troops at Hot Springs, Ladakh on the same day in 1959. On Wednesday, Shah placed a wreath at the National Police Memorial to honour the service and sacrifice by 36,852 police personnel who have made the supreme sacrifice thus far.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah says peace has been established in Jammu and Kashmir, northeast region and areas affected by Left-wing extremism. Shah said 2026 has been an extremely significant year for the Indian police, as they successfully freed the country from the decades-old stranglehold of violent Naxalism.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
