Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf lost $3 million on $23 million Tiburon mansion after four years of searching for a buyer
Article Text:
Steffi Graf-Andre Agassi (Getty Images)

Andre Agassi's Tiburon estate took years to sell

Why the luxury home struggled to attract buyers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2006, tennis legends Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf made a costly decision involving one of their most impressive real estate assets. After nearly four years on the market, the couple finally found a buyer for their sprawling Tiburon estate in California. The property attracted attention for its breathtaking views, luxury features and celebrity connections. Yet the final sale price came in below what Agassi had paid five years earlier. The deal showed that even a high-end property in a sought-after location can struggle to find the right buyer when its upkeep and price become difficult to justify.Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf agreed to sell the 3.5-acre estate for $20 million, around $3 million less than the $23 million Agassi reportedly paid in 2001. The sale was expected to close in the first week of January 2007, according to Bill Bullock, whose firm represented the couple.The property offered plenty of space and privacy. It featured a 10,500-square-foot main house, separate staff quarters measuring 2,500 square feet, two swimming pools, a stream and a tennis court. Its elevated setting also provided views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the San Francisco skyline.However, the estate's size came with significant carrying costs. Agassi's family rarely used the property, and his financial advisers wanted him to sell it rather than continue paying to maintain a largely vacant home.The original asking price stood at $24.5 million. After several reductions, Agassi lowered it to $21 million about six months before the reported deal. Bullock explained why the couple became more flexible on price."When they considered the annual cost of that property to sit there vacant, they decided that they needed a little inducement for the marketplace and they started reducing the price."..The final $20 million offer still ranked among the Bay Area's most expensive home sales that year. Stuart Peterson, president of hedge fund Artis Capital Management, agreed to buy the estate. His fund had also been a major investor in YouTube before Google's $1.65 billion acquisition of the video-sharing company.Despite its impressive setting, the Tiburon property had a drawback. Built in 1976, the house had not received a major renovation since the mid-1990s. That left parts of the estate feeling dated to prospective buyers, making it harder to compete in the luxury market.Bill Bullock said several wealthy visitors, including movie stars, had toured the home but ultimately passed on it. The buyer planned to make changes, although details were not disclosed before the transaction closed.Andre Agassi had wanted the property for years. He first considered buying it in the mid-1990s while married to actress Brooke Shields, but she disliked the compound and discouraged the purchase. When it returned to the market, Agassi acted quickly rather than risk losing it again.By 2006, Agassi had retired from professional tennis and was living in Las Vegas with Graf and their two children. The couple were also exploring property development, including a luxury condo-hotel project in Idaho. Their Tiburon sale marked a shift away from a costly home they seldom used, even as they pursued new opportunities in real estate.
Article Summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf agreed to sell the 3.5-acre estate for $20 million. The sale was expected to close in the first week of January 2007. The property featured a 10,500-square-foot main house, separate staff quarters and two swimming pools.

Article Title: Jordan Clarkson's 10,106-square-foot Texas mansion hits the market for $7.5 million in 2026 with a private basketball court and cinema
Article Text:
Jordan Clarkson's 10,106-square-foot Texas mansion hits the market for $7.5 million in 2026(Getty)

Jordan Clarkson's mansion has a private basketball court , cinema and four-car garage

Why Jordan Clarkson's San Antonio mansion is listed for $7.5 million

Jordan Clarkson's San Antonio roots go back to his childhood Spurs memories

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jordan Clarkson’s San Antonio mansion is back on the market, and the $7.5 million listing comes with several features built for life beyond the basketball court. The three-storey property covers 10,106 square feet in The Dominion, a gated community in his hometown.It has a private half basketball court, a cinema with stadium-style seating, an infinity-edge pool and a detached guesthouse with a full bar. Clarkson acquired the house in January 2023 through JClarkson Enterprises LLC.The estate stands on a 1.12-acre lot at Crescent Park in The Dominion. Built in 2008, the Mediterranean-style property has five bedrooms, six full bathrooms and one half-bathroom. The listing describes a home designed for entertaining, with dedicated spaces for recreation, dining and relaxation.The half basketball court is one of its defining features. Clarkson can shoot at home without leaving the property, while the indoor theater offers stadium-style seating and a hardwood concession counter. A separate game room gives the house another entertainment area, and a wine lounge provides a dedicated space for drinks and hosting guests. The property also has an elevator connecting its levels.The main bedroom is among the home's largest rooms. Realtor.com lists its dimensions as 24 by 16 feet and notes that it has outdoor access, a sitting area and a walk-in closet.Its bathroom measures 15 by 18 feet and has separate vanities and a separate tub and shower. These details give prospective buyers a clearer idea of how the estate is laid out beyond its overall square footage.The kitchen has professional-grade appliances, custom cabinetry and an island. The listing also identifies a separate dining room, an eat-in kitchen, a breakfast bar and a walk-in pantry. Three or more fireplaces are listed among the home's features, including wood-burning and gas options.The outdoor amenities extend beyond the basketball court. The property has a private swimming pool with an infinity edge, a spa and an Italian wood-burning pizza oven. A stainless-steel Viking gas grill is also mentioned in the earlier property report. The detached casita gives visitors a separate place to stay, with its own bathroom, sitting area and full bar. Its lower level includes a gym and a full bathroom.There is also an attached garage with space for at least four cars, plus additional storage. Realtor.com lists mature trees, landscaped grounds and views of the city and a bluff among the property's features. The Dominion community itself lists controlled and guarded access, a golf course, tennis facilities, a clubhouse, parks and jogging trails among its amenities.The property's price has a history. Texas attorney Thomas J. Henry owned the estate before selling it in January 2023. He had listed the home for $7.5 million, the same asking price Clarkson's property now carries. The San Antonio Express-News reported at the time that public records linked the buyer, JClarkson Enterprises LLC, to Clarkson. The final sale price was not disclosed.One figure from that transaction should not be mistaken for the purchase price. According to the Express-News, JClarkson Enterprises LLC borrowed $3.78 million from City National Bank for the acquisition. That was the reported loan amount, not confirmation of what Clarkson paid for the house. The public reporting does not establish the final purchase price, so it is not possible to calculate his profit or loss from the current listing.The present listing identifies Janay Bankston of Barlowe Daly Realty as the listing agent. Realtor.com showed the property at $7.5 million and listed a homeowners association fee of $295 per month. Its listing also gave an annual property-tax figure of $120,234 for tax year 2026. Those carrying costs sit alongside the asking price for anyone assessing the full expense of owning the estate.Clarkson has not publicly explained why he is selling the house. The available reporting does not establish whether the decision is connected to his basketball career, another property purchase or a personal reason. The listing price also does not guarantee that the home will sell for that amount.The property is in the city where Clarkson attended Karen J. Wagner High School. He grew up watching the Spurs during their championship years, long before he entered the NBA. In June 2026, while preparing to face San Antonio in the NBA Finals with the New York Knicks, Clarkson spoke about the memories he had of the team's title celebrations.“My stepmom worked at the Westin, so I would see the parades through the hotel balconies and stuff. I would sneak around there,” Clarkson said during NBA Finals media availability on June 2, 2026. He recalled that visiting NBA teams stayed at the downtown hotel, giving him opportunities to take pictures with players and ask for autographs. “I was definitely that kid,” he added.Clarkson also recalled how the city came alive during the Spurs' Finals appearances. “Around to see this energy and see how alive the city comes when the Spurs are in the Finals and winning championships. It's a great experience,” he said.The remarks offered a personal look at his connection to San Antonio while he prepared to compete against the franchise he had followed as a child.That hometown history is separate from the real estate decision. Clarkson has not said that his memories of San Antonio influenced the sale, and there is no confirmed explanation for his plans for the house. The listing itself offers the clearest details: a 10,106-square-foot property in The Dominion, a private basketball court, a theater, an infinity-edge pool and a detached casita, all offered at $7.5 million.
Article Summary: The three-storey property covers 10,106 square feet in The Dominion, a gated community in his hometown. It has a private half basketball court, a cinema with stadium-style seating, an infinity-edge pool and a detached guesthouse with a full bar. Clarkson acquired the house in January 2023 through JClarkson Enterprises LLC.

Article Title: India moves to develop its first indigenous aviation gun for Prachand, Rudra combat helicopters
Article Text:
An Indian Air Force Prachand Light Combat Helicopter fires 70mm rockets during a training exercise. (Image Credit: IAF)

India’s 30kW Laser Weapon: DRDO’s ‘Drone Killer’ Is Coming to Replace Missiles

In an effort that will increase indigenous content in the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand and , the Defence Research and Development Organisation's ( DRDO ) Armament Research and Development Establishment (ARDE) have shortlisted domestic firms SSS Defence and Kalyani Group to develop an indigenous 20mm aviation gun and turret system for the Army and Air Force's Rudra and Prachand combat helicopters, in a move to reduce dependence on foreign weapon suppliers. This will mark India's first effort to design and develop an aviation medium-caliber aviation gun domestically.The development phase is expected to take around two years, after which production orders will be placed following acceptance procedures. The order will be divided between the two companies based on cost calculations, with the lowest bidder set to receive 60% of the order and the other company 40%. ARDE and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) had signed a memorandum of understanding last year to collaborate on the project.The gun is intended for HAL's Advanced Light Helicopter Mk-IV, known as Rudra, and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand. Both platforms are designed to engage ground targets and support troops using a combination of guns, rockets and missiles. The Rudra can carry a 20mm turret gun, 70mm rocket pods and missiles, while the Prachand's weapon suite includes a 20mm gun, rockets and anti-tank guided missiles. The Indian Army has previously conducted day and night firing trials of the LCH's turret gun.The LCH currently uses the THL20 turret manufactured by European defence company KNDS. In September, KNDS announced that it would supply 126 newly manufactured 20mm THL20 turrets for India's new LCH fleet. The company has also supplied 136 THL20 turrets for Advanced Light Helicopters operated by the Indian Air Force. The indigenous development programme would provide an alternative to imported systems.The gun programme is progressing alongside efforts to indigenise the helicopters' other weapons. The indigenous HELINA and Dhruvastra anti-tank guided missiles, derived from the Nag missile programme, are intended for Army and Air Force helicopter operations respectively. In June, Bharat Dynamics Limited received orders worth Rs 1,109.37 crore from HAL for HELINA launchers and associated line-replaceable units. A separate order worth Rs 238.34 crore covered countermeasure dispensing system line-replaceable units. The contracts are scheduled for execution over 24 to 60 months.India is also preparing to manufacture 70mm rockets domestically through a collaboration between Kalyani Strategic Systems and Thales Belgium. Announced in September, the agreement combines Thales' technical expertise with Kalyani's manufacturing and testing infrastructure. The first fully assembled rocket produced in India is expected in early 2027. The rockets can be launched from aircraft, ground platforms and naval systems.The indigenous gun, missile and rocket programmes would expand domestic manufacturing across the Rudra and Prachand weapon systems. However, the new gun remains at the development stage, while the missile and rocket programmes have their own production and delivery timelines.
Article Summary: The gun is intended for HAL's Advanced Light Helicopter Mk-IV, known as Rudra, and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand. India is also preparing to manufacture 70mm rockets domestically through a collaboration between Kalyani Strategic Systems and Thales Belgium.

Article Title: Season’s Greetings: Delhi sees most polluted day after Dussehra in 5 years, GRAP invoked
Article Text:
Delhi's air quality has worsened, now at an AQI of 245 (Representative image)

GRAP-1 measures kick in





NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to poor for the first time this season as the AQI climbed to 245 Wednesday. It was 179 a day earlier.Delhi also saw the most polluted day after Dussehra in the last five years. An AQI higher than Wednesday’s was last recorded in 2021, when it was 284 the day after Dussehra.The air quality worsened due to unfavourable meteorological conditions and additional emissions from firecrackers that were burst during Dussehra celebrations. The contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s PM2.5 was 3.9% Wednesday.The deterioration in air quality prompted Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke Stage I of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).This includes a ban on the entry of intercity and inter-state buses from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and J&K that are below BS-VI standards and run on neither electricity nor CNG. Regulations on the use of diesel generator (DG) sets also kicked in.GRAP Stage I also asks for augmenting public transport through CNG and electric buses, metro and RRTS services by inducting an additional fleet and increasing the frequency of service.Delhi Metro will run 20 additional trips from Thursday onwards for all weekdays.“The forecast by India Meteorological Department and Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology has also predicted that AQI will remain in the poor category in the coming days,” CAQM said.The commission added that actions under Stage I of GRAP will be implemented, monitored and reviewed by all the agencies in NCR to ensure that the AQI does not rise further.Central Pollution Control Board’s data shows that air quality showed a rising trend since early Wednesday. The AQI was 227 at 7am and touched 245 at 4pm, when CPCB releases its 24-hour average AQI bulletin. It increased to 248 at 8pm.This year, a higher AQI than 245 was last witnessed on July 24 at 246 in the poor category when dust travelled from Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan towards north-west India.The AQI was in the very poor category at seven locations Wednesday -- Pusa (329), Chandni Chowk (326), Jahangirpuri (313), Punjabi Bagh (312), Patparganj (304), Mandir Marg (303) and Vivek Vihar (302).Mahesh Palawat, vice-president of Skymet Meteorology, said the worsening air quality could be attributed to the Dussehra celebrations, including the burning of the Ravana effigies.“Falling night temperatures and light winds may have further contributed to the deterioration.... Traffic emissions, industrial smoke and dust tend to accumulate under such conditions, while fireworks during the celebrations may also have contributed to the overnight rise in pollution. The haze observed Wednesday followed Tuesday’s celebrations,” he said.The Decision Support System (DSS), which functions under the Union ministry of earth sciences, has estimated that the contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s pollution could rise to 7.4% Thursday, 15.9% Friday and 4.1% Saturday.Sunil Dahiya, founder of the think tank Envirocatalyst, said: “The slow moving wind coming from the northwest, bringing more emission load from farm fires and festive emission load, Tuesday evening to night,” had added to other regional sources as well as emissions from within Delhi.In Oct last year, the AQI worsened to poor on Oct 14. It was 211. It deteriorated to very poor by Oct 20 at 345 last year. Delhi Traffic Police has urged commuters to reduce vehicular emissions. It advised people to use the metro and public transport, carpool and avoid unnecessary trips, maintain their vehicles and keep valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs).
Article Summary: Delhi also saw the most polluted day after Dussehra in the last five years. The contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s PM2.5 was 3.9% Wednesday. The deterioration in air quality prompted Commission for Air Quality Management to invoke Stage I of the Graded Response Action Plan.

Article Title: Mumbai clears 77 of 231 garbage hotspots, targets 128 by year-end
Article Text:
BMC is actively addressing garbage-vulnerable points in Mumbai by cleaning and transforming these spaces into public areas.

Continuous monitoring and presence of staff have been established to maintain cleanliness in these improved areas.





MUMBAI: From reclaiming footpaths riddled with illegal construction debris to creating seating areas for senior citizens, BMC is attempting to turn Mumbai's garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs) into usable public spaces.Of the 231 such spots identified across the city till April this year, 77 had been cleaned up by Oct, leaving 154. The civic body has set a target of bringing the number down to 128 by Dec. A garbage-vulnerable point is a location where waste is repeatedly dumped and accumulates over a prolonged period, requiring intervention by the concerned civic ward to address the problem.Two such locations are in Sewri and Chinchpokli areas wherein the civic body is attempting to go beyond simply clearing accumulated waste. At Zakaria Bunder Road along Eastern Freeway, a spot where construction and demolition (C&D) waste was being dumped illegally at night has been cleared, restoring the footpath for safer and more convenient pedestrian movement.A CCTV now has been placed there as well. Shiv Sena UBT corporator Bharti Pednekar said at Chinchpokli, another GVP has been eliminated and the space converted into a seating area, with benches now placed at the site."The facility gives elderly residents a place to sit, relax and interact with one another. We have even spoken to the locals to ensure they dispose waste the correct way," she said.However, sustaining these improvements remains a challenge, particularly in neighbourhoods where dumping garbage at the same location has become a long-standing practice. Assistant Municipal Commissioner of F-South ward Vrushali Ingole said eliminating GVPs requires residents to cooperate with the civic body and hand over their waste directly to BMC collection vans rather than dumping it on roadsides."The ward first deploys staff at an identified spot for a few days to understand where the garbage is coming from. Our teams then approach residents in the surrounding areas, explain the need to stop dumping waste at the location and seek their cooperation. We have also arranged for collection vans to stop at convenient points so residents can hand over their garbage directly," she said.Sanjay Mohite, assistant engineer of F-South's solid waste department, said at the Eastern Freeway location, the ward set up a Solid Waste Management chowky to ensure staff presence and prevent the spot from reverting to a dumping ground. "The footpath was also improved and greenery added to discourage fresh dumping. "Sustained monitoring and public cooperation will be crucial to keeping the spaces clean," said deputy municipal commissioner Kiran Dighavkar.
Article Summary: BMC is attempting to turn Mumbai's garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs) into usable public spaces. Of 231 such spots identified across the city till April this year, 77 had been cleaned up by Oct, leaving 154. The civic body has set a target of bringing the number down to 128 by Dec.

Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has revealed plans for a significant chemical park adjacent to Vadhvan Port





MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port and urged the Centre to approve the project, for which the state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres.Speaking at the inauguration of Indochem in Goregaon, Fadnavis said the state government would make the land available for the proposed park and asked the Centre to sanction the project.The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.Union minister for chemicals and fertilisers JP Nadda said the Centre had already announced the Bhavya Rasayan scheme in the Union Budget. Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Google co-founder Larry Page is the richest tech titan to leave California ahead of Billionaire's tax vote: How his exit may dent state’s $100 billion tax target
Article Text:
Moving entities to Delaware and buying big in Miami

The $29 billion dent in Prop 40’s target

With Californians set to vote in just a few weeks on Proposition 40 – a measure proposing a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires – Google co-founder Larry Page has emerged as the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections as he will be the richest techie to leave the state. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026. While a few prominent executives, such as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, have stated they are "perfectly fine" with the proposal, multiple ultra-wealthy residents chose to exit before the January deadline.Chief among them is the 53-year-old Page. Holding an estimated net worth of $292 billion, Page had deep roots in California spanning decades, Fortune reported, adding that had he remained a California resident past the cutoff date, he would have owed an estimated $15 billion under the one-time tax levy.State filings have revealed that Page began unwinding his operational and personal presence in California late last year.According to an analysis of corporate records reported by Fortune, Page’s family office, Koop, was transferred out of California and officially incorporated in Delaware in late December. Multiple associated entities, including Flu Lab LLC, One Aero and Oceankind, followed the same route, moving their registrations from California to Delaware during the same month.Simultaneously, Page redirected significant capital toward luxury real estate on the East Coast. The Wall Street Journal reported that Page acquired two premier estates in Miami for a combined $173.4 million, which includes Coconut Grove Estate ($101.5 million, 11,855-square-foot property) and a neighboring parcel purchased for $71.9 million.The departures of top-tier billionaires have already weakened the potential financial yield of the ballot measure. Prop 40 was projected to generate roughly $100 billion for the state. However, according to an estimate by Fortune, just four departed tech leaders – Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Peter Thiel and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick – would have collectively owed approximately $29 billion. Their relocations before the residency cutoff mean the state has effectively lost out on more than a quarter of the measure's total projected revenue pool before ballots are even counted.Elon Musk, the richest person in the world, moved to Texas in 2020. Meanwhile, Jeff Bezos who recently but briefly secured the second richest person spot, departed Seattle for Miami in late 2023, eventually selling his Hunts Point home for a record $63 million to live in a $237 million Miami compound with his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos.
Article Summary: Google co-founder Larry Page is the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026.

Article Title: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is very happy with airlines deal with Starlink, says helping us get customers; Elon Musk responds
Article Text:
Elon Musk Starlink

Elon Musk: 'Starlink moves the needle'

Earnings miss amid higher fuel costs

Ongoing debate with Delta Air Lines

Scott Kirby, the CEO of United Airlines is already noticing customers switch from rival carriers because of its partnership with Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. According to the remarks made during a CNBC interview and the company's latest earnings discussion, the airline views the rollout as a key competitive advantage. Kirby highlighted that the carrier is expected to cross the milestone of having Starlink installed on more than 50% of its flights this week and that the entire fleet is expected to be equipped with the service by the end of next year, according to a Benzinga report citing the interview. "We already see customers moving from other airlines today," Kirby said when discussing the impact of the onboard internet service. However, he added that it remains unclear whether the benefit will be large enough on its own to help deliver double-digit profit margins.Kirby's comments quickly drew a response from Musk on X. Replying to a post that highlighted the interview, the billionaire wrote: "Starlink moves the needle." The exchange adds to Musk's long-running efforts to promote Starlink's aviation offering as a key differentiator for airlines seeking to improve onboard connectivity. United Airlines calls Starlink a 'tailwind'Speaking during the airline's earnings call, Kirby described Starlink as a "tailwind" for the company and said United has launched a tracking tool that allows passengers to check whether their upcoming flight is equipped with the service.Kirby also expressed confidence that the airline is building a significant lead over competitors."We're on our way to being the only global U.S. airline with Starlink at scale. A lot of new customers are going to try us. It's a huge head start," he said, according to the Benzinga report. The comments suggest that United views onboard connectivity as more than just a passenger convenience feature, seeing it instead as a tool for attracting and retaining travellers.The remarks came as United reported quarterly earnings that fell slightly short of Wall Street expectations. The airline posted earnings of $2.54 per share, below analyst estimates of $2.59 per share. Revenue of $17.875 billion also narrowly missed the consensus forecast of $17.888 billion.United said fuel expenses rose by $1.8 billion year-over-year, driven largely by energy market disruptions linked to the Iran war. During the earnings call, Kirby warned that elevated oil prices could continue to pressure the airline industry over the next year.He also said that between six and 10 U.S. airlines could lose money this year if fuel costs remain high and geopolitical tensions continue to affect energy markets.The latest comments come against the backdrop of an ongoing debate between Musk and Delta Air Lines over inflight internet connectivity. Delta has chosen to deploy Amazon's Project Kuiper-based internet service on its aircraft instead of Starlink. Musk has repeatedly criticised the decision, arguing that airlines risk losing customers by not adopting Starlink's network.In previous comments, Musk warned that Delta could lose passengers because of its decision and even mocked the carrier's onboard connectivity, claiming a flight without reliable internet would be an ideal place to isolate an AI model from online access.With United now publicly stating that Starlink is already helping attract customers from competing airlines, the debate over satellite-powered inflight internet appears set to intensify.
Article Summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says Starlink is already helping attract customers from rival carriers. Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, is expected to be installed on more than 50% of the airline's flights this week. Kirby's comments quickly drew a response from Musk on X.

Article Title: Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of job cuts; starting this month, layoffs are part of what CEO Asha Sharma described as 'fundamental reset of how Xbox operates and invests'
Article Text:
'Fundamental reset' of Xbox operations

Xbox job cuts: Employees demoralised

Studios and strategy under review

Why Xbox is being reset

Questions about Xbox’s future

Microsoft’s Xbox division is reportedly preparing for three additional rounds of layoffs over the coming months as CEO Asha Sharma pushed ahead with a sweeping restructuring aimed at improving the gaming business’ financial performance. According to a report by Fortune, Sharma is planning some more job cuts this month, followed by some additional rounds in November and January, extending a shake-up that has already resulted in thousands of layoffs across Microsoft’s gaming operations. In July this year, Asha Sharman announced plans to eliminate approximately 3,200 jobs during Microsoft's fiscal 2027, including around 1,600 positions that were cut immediately. A further round of layoffs affecting roughly 260 employees followed in September. Microsoft has not publicly confirmed the latest reported plans or disclosed how many employees could be affected.The layoffs are part of what Asha Sharma has previously described as a fundamental reset of how Xbox operates and invests. In a message to employees earlier this year, she said the business was not healthy and acknowledged that Xbox was operating with margins significantly below those of comparable platform and publishing companies.Sharma argued that years of heavy investment in content, hardware, platforms and studio acquisitions had failed to deliver the level of growth Microsoft expected. The restructuring is aimed at simplifying the organisation, reducing costs and focusing resources on projects with stronger commercial prospects.Spreading the cuts over several waves has left some employees demoralised, Fortune reports. Some staff feel they are working under a yearlong cloud, waiting to see whether their roles will be next. Fortune also found at least one employee who was laid off and then offered a chance to stay. Some employees appreciated Sharma’s transparency, the report says. Sharma acknowledged the tough decisions but said she values people and does not intend to be transactional.The reset has already resulted in major changes across Microsoft's gaming portfolio. Studios including Double Fine Productions and Compulsion Games have been allowed to regain independence, while other teams have undergone reviews, reorganisations or ownership discussions as Xbox streamlines its operations.The restructuring reflects growing pressure on Microsoft's gaming division to improve profitability amid rising industry costs and a challenging console market. While speculation has emerged over Xbox's long-term future within Microsoft, Sharma recently told media outlets that Xbox is not for sale, while Microsoft executives have publicly backed her leadership of the gaming business.Sharma, 38, took over in February from longtime Xbox head Phil Spencer. She had no video game industry experience, having previously led product work on Microsoft’s AI Foundry platform. Fortune describes Xbox as a roughly $21 billion business with profit margins of about 3 percent, a fraction of what rivals earn and far below what Microsoft expects of its major units. Current Xbox consoles have sold only a little over a third as many units as the PlayStation 5, according to third-party estimates, and memory chip shortages are pushing up hardware costs. Sharma told Fortune in July that Xbox had grown by making many bets and lost focus on its core business, saying the company “spread ourselves too thin.”Several current and former staff members told Fortune they believe Xbox is being prepared for a possible sale, spinoff or other restructuring, amid heavy Microsoft spending on artificial intelligence. Judson Althoff, one of Microsoft’s most senior executives, rejected that idea, saying Microsoft would not have put Sharma in charge of a business it intends to sell. The next test comes with Microsoft’s quarterly earnings report this month, and Sharma has said she expects financial improvements to show in Microsoft’s fiscal 2027.
Article Summary: Microsoft's Xbox division is reportedly preparing for three additional rounds of layoffs over the coming months. CEO Asha Sharma is pushing ahead with a sweeping restructuring aimed at improving the gaming business’ financial performance. In July this year, Asha Sharman announced plans to eliminate approximately 3,200 jobs during Microsoft's fiscal 2027.

Article Title: Michael Dell built one of the world’s biggest computer companies; his daughter Kira chose water sustainability and became CEO of an Austin startup
Article Text:
Kira Dell ’s career in water sustainability leads to CEO role at Adaptive Water

Kira Dell takes a different career path from Michael Dell

Kira’s work in Texas extends beyond her company

Dell siblings pursue separate business ventures

How Michael and Susan Dell raised their four children

Michael Dell built his fortune by turning a personal computer business into one of the world’s largest technology companies. His daughter Kira has chosen a different industry, taking on a problem that has little to do with selling computers. Based in Austin, Texas, she became chief executive of Adaptive Water in 2025, a company focused on improving the sustainability of the state’s water supply. Her career began in teaching before moving into product management, eventually leading her into the water sector. While her father’s business grew around computer hardware and enterprise technology, Kira has concentrated on a resource that communities, industries and households depend on every day.Kira Dell’s route to the executive role began outside the technology industry. She graduated from Vassar College in 2015 with a degree in international studies, according to her LinkedIn profile. Her education also included study at the School for International Training and the University of Alaska Fairbanks.She initially worked as a teacher before moving into product management, a role that brought her into the development and organisation of products and services.That experience preceded her move into the water sector. In 2025, she became chief executive of Adaptive Water, an Austin-based company working to advance water sustainability in Texas.Adaptive Water’s stated aim is to help accelerate the state’s transition towards more sustainable water use. Kira’s role puts her at the head of a business addressing that challenge, rather than in the technology sector where her father built his career. The available biographical information does not suggest that she followed a conventional route through Dell Technologies before taking the position.Michael Dell founded the company that became Dell Technologies in 1984, initially building computers around a direct-sales model. The business expanded over the following decades, becoming a major supplier of personal computers, servers and other technology used by individuals and organisations. Its growth established Michael as one of the wealthiest figures in the industry.Kira’s work at Adaptive Water represents a clear difference in professional focus. Rather than developing hardware or technology infrastructure, she leads a company concerned with the management of a natural resource. Water sustainability involves its own commercial and operational demands, including finding practical ways to address supply pressures and support more efficient use.Alongside her position at Adaptive Water, Kira serves on the board of Texas Water Trade, an organisation involved in water-related issues in the state. The role connects her corporate work with a broader network concerned with water management and sustainability.Her career has moved through education and product management into executive leadership, with water becoming its central focus. Public information about her professional background is more limited than the record of her father’s career, but her appointment as chief executive in 2025 marked a significant step in her own business life.The Dell family remains closely associated with technology through Michael’s company and his public profile. Kira’s work, however, is centred on a different challenge facing Texas. At Adaptive Water, she is leading a business seeking to make the state’s water use more sustainable, in a field where the demands of households, businesses and communities must be considered together.Her brother Zach has also pursued an entrepreneurial career in Austin, although in a separate area. He graduated from the University of Southern California in 2019, studying social sciences, psychology and economics, before beginning his career in private equity. In 2023, he co-founded Base Power Company, which provides residential battery systems designed to supply electricity during outages and support the wider grid during periods of high demand.Michael and Susan Dell married in 1989 and raised four children together: Alexa, Kira, Juliette and Zach. The family made its home in Austin, where the Dells lived on a large estate known as The Castle. Michael’s work at Dell Technologies placed him among the most prominent figures in the technology industry, but his children were not expected to follow an identical route simply because of the family name.In an October 2025 interview with Timeless Partners, Michael described how the household operated despite the financial comfort his success provided. He said the children were expected to earn or save for the things they wanted rather than assume their parents would provide them. The approach, he explained, involved maintaining rules and expectations at home, even when the family had the means to make life easier.
Article Summary: Kira Dell became chief executive of Adaptive Water in 2025. The company is focused on improving the sustainability of the state's water supply. Her career began in teaching before moving into product management. Her brother Zach has also pursued an entrepreneurial career in Austin.
